# Purpose

Award credit for a defensible cantilever idealization, complete free-body diagram, correct internal resultants, accurate hollow-section properties, correct use of the flexure formula, and a concise engineering assessment bounded by the stated assumptions.

# Scope of the Base Problem

The base model assumes static loading, a straight prismatic arm, a concentrated occupant/seat force, linear-elastic material response, small deformation, plane sections remaining plane, and concentric inner and outer rectangles. It neglects arm and hardware self-weight unless included in P, local weld and bolt stresses, bracket flexibility, contact effects, stress concentrations, fatigue, impact, vibration, and dynamic occupant loading. No allowable stress is assigned, so the final assessment interprets demand and geometry sensitivity without claiming a complete pass/fail verification.

# Supplemental Assessment Structure

- context interpretation and load path: 20%;
- student idealization and assumptions: 20%;
- internal loading and section properties: 30%;
- bending stress and stress sense: 20%;
- engineering assessment and limitations: 10%.
